names_for.catalogue_side: Data Products on the 'Licensed Data Marketplace' (tiers include 'Premium Data' and the free 'Open Data Repository')
names_for.custom_side: 'Request a Dataset' / 'Request Data'; in the docs, sourcing 'bespoke data requirements'; in the fee schedule, 'bespoke brokerage or enterprise transactions'

operator_role.note: Opendatabay is authorised as the provider's (by default non-exclusive) broker and collects payment, but the provider is licensor of record under the provider's licence.

economics_model.note: Sliding per-transaction commission, 30% down to 5%; no listing fee.

supply_models.note: public_or_scraped = free datasets republished by an account named Opendatabay Labs from public sources; no evidence of the operator's own commissioned or speculative collection.

custody_model.note: Instant download on the platform for some listings; provider-delivered (S3, API, cloud credentials, FTP) for others. Where downloads are hosted is not stated.

public_prices.note: Every listing card viewed showed a price or 'Free', but larger batches and bespoke deals are unpriced.

licence_model.note: Provider picks one of two Opendatabay AI-training templates, a standard open licence or its own custom licence.

exclusivity_offered.note: Exclusivity in the terms is provider-to-broker only; no buyer-side exclusive licence offered or excluded.

buyer_vetting.note: What buyer 'onboarding' involves is not published.

sample_mechanics.note: Samples depend on the provider; the listings viewed had no sample tab.

versioning.note: Listings show only a last-updated date; nothing on revisions or what past buyers receive.

human_subject_consent_docs.note: Consent is warranted by the provider and records stay with the provider; nothing obliges release evidence to reach the buyer.

contributor_pay_model.note: Only registered businesses sell; Opendatabay has no individual contributors and says nothing on how providers pay their capturers.

erasure_after_sale.note: Deletion duty exists only in Opendatabay's two AI-training licences; CC-licensed or custom-licensed listings carry no such duty.

quality_evidence.note: A 5/5 'UDTR' trust rating shows on listings, but who assigns it and how is not published.

Q1.answer: Opendatabay claims 30k+ users and 23K+ downloads (vendor-stated) and runs a public request board, but its 'who is buying data' article is a placeholder; no buyer units or volumes are published.

Q2.answer: Listing costs nothing upfront and the operator pushes listings to search engines and LLMs and markets them; in return the provider cannot deal off-platform with introduced buyers and may grant exclusive brokerage.

Q3.answer: Inventory comes from verified registered businesses that warrant they created the data or hold all rights; an account named Opendatabay Labs also republishes public data for free. Individuals are barred as sellers, though marketing copy says otherwise.

Q4.answer: Nothing found on carving resale rights out of commissioned work, or on retroactive term changes beyond 'continued use constitutes acceptance'.

Q5.answer: Opendatabay is the provider's broker and 'conduit, not the licensor'; the provider is licensor, warrants rights and lawful collection, and indemnifies Opendatabay. Liability is capped at platform fees.

Q6.answer: Mixed: instant download for some listings, and the provider delivers others by S3, API, cloud credentials or negotiated means. The docs call Opendatabay 'not a data warehouse'.

Q7.answer: The provider warrants lawful, ethical and consented collection and keeps consent records; PII must be anonymised. No clause addresses people depicted, model or property releases, or capturer consent to onward sale.

Q8.answer: Opendatabay's AI licences are non-exclusive and perpetual, ban redistribution and watermark removal, and require deletion on request or termination; audits are limited to once a year. Listing labels (CC0, CC BY) can contradict those restrictions.

Q9.answer: Self-serve 'Buy Now' checkout at provider-set prices, plus negotiated and bespoke deals. Opendatabay takes a sliding commission of 30% down to 5% out of the seller's proceeds.

Q10.answer: A listing ('data product') has licence, AI-licence, delivery, type and last-updated fields; buyers buy once or subscribe. Delisting does not affect executed sales. No revision or version model is described.

Q11.answer: Before paying, buyers see the licence, metadata, a trust rating and a provider badge, and registered users can download provider samples. Providers are KYB-verified, but listing accuracy is the provider's responsibility.

Q12.answer: The catalogue of 'data products' sits alongside 'Request a Dataset', where Opendatabay says its provider network helps find or create data, and the fee schedule allows separate terms for bespoke brokerage.

sections.positioning: A UK company (incorporated May 2024, one director) running a 'Licensed Data Marketplace for AI Training' [c010, c007, c008]. It calls itself 'a marketplace and commercial brokerage platform, not a data warehouse' [c016]. Claimed scale is modest: 586 products and 91 providers [c011, c012]. Its company was briefly gazetted for strike-off in April 2026 before the action was discontinued, after late accounts [c004, c005, c006].
sections.supply: Supply is third-party businesses only: KYC/KYB checks, and individuals barred [c056, c057, c119], although the about page and resources hub still address individuals [c019, c181]. Providers warrant they are the creator or hold all rights [c075]. An 'Opendatabay Labs' account republishes public data for free [c172, c174]. Image and video supply includes a 220K-hour egocentric video set [c150].
sections.object_model: The unit is a 'data product' with fields for licence, a separate AI-training licence, delivery method, dataset type and last-updated date [c122, c123, c124, c125, c126]. Pages show listed and updated dates and view counts [c162]. No revision model is described.
sections.listing: Profiles and listings are public [c062]. Providers must disclose limitations and biases and are told to write 'Unknown' rather than omit [c030, c129]. Opendatabay may suggest listing changes [c031].
sections.discovery: Opendatabay says listings are auto-indexed by search engines and exposed to LLMs, and it offers AI search with a match score [c116, c117, c118]. It may use provider names and banners in marketing [c071].
sections.trust: Listings show a 5/5 'Universal Data Trust Rating' and a 'Licensed LLM Data Provider' badge, but how the rating is set is unpublished [c157, c158, c161]. The terms disclaim accuracy and put it on providers [c091, c184].
sections.transaction: Paid listings have 'Buy Now'; purchase types are one-time, subscription, pay-per-use and managed access [c167, c099, c100, c101]. Payments go through third-party processors [c088]. Off-platform dealing with introduced buyers is banned [c065].
sections.pricing: Providers set prices [c026]. Commission is per transaction, 30% at GBP 1-100 sliding to 5% above GBP 250,000, deducted from seller proceeds [c038, c044, c048]. There is no listing fee, and a GBP 100 payout minimum [c052, c053]. Listed prices reach GBP 371,000 for 50,000 hours of egocentric video [c151, c152].
sections.licence: The provider is licensor and picks the licence: Opendatabay's General or Commercial AI-training licence, a standard licence, or its own [c024, c027, c135]. The Commercial licence is non-exclusive and perpetual and bans redistribution [c137, c138]. Listing labels can contradict this: a CC0 label beside a no-redistribution clause [c166, c183].
sections.custody: Custody is mixed. The docs describe provider delivery to the customer environment [c096], instant download [c160], S3 or custom delivery [c155] and cloud credentials [c107]. Providers own security and availability [c032].
sections.vetting: Providers pass KYB in 1-2 business days, including 'data product suitability' [c057, c120, c121]. Opendatabay may demand proof of ownership, audit sources and quality, and remove products [c082, c067, c083, c084]. Buyers face only registration [c090].
sections.contributor_pay: Not applicable: sellers are registered businesses and individuals cannot list [c119]. Payouts go to verified business accounts [c061].
sections.post_sale: Delisting does not affect executed sales, and pending sales must still be delivered [c033, c034]. The AI licences require deletion on termination or the licensor's request [c140]. Refunds are excluded once access is granted [c087]. In disputes, Opendatabay is a 'neutral intermediary' [c113].
sections.catalogue_custom: 'Request a Dataset' sits beside the catalogue: Opendatabay says its provider network helps 'find or create' data [c177, c178], and it can set separate terms for bespoke brokerage [c049].
sections.changes: Terms dated 2026: Brokerage & Listing, Provider and Right to List (27 February), Terms of Service (26 July) and the fee schedule (24 August) [c086, c002]. Every document may change at any time on continued use [c051].
sections.demand: Only vendor figures exist: 30k+ users and 23K+ downloads [c013, c014]. A public request board lists requests from researchers, developers and businesses [c179].
sections.regulation: English law. The Terms of Service send disputes to arbitration, while the Listing Terms name the London courts [c094, c186]. The Commercial licence has the licensor represent GDPR compliance [c143].

buyer_journey.step: Lands on the homepage ('Licensed Data Marketplace for AI Training and LLM Fine-Tuning') showing 586 products and 91 providers.
Browses categories (AI training, robotics/egocentric, premium, government, synthetic) or searches in natural language with match scores; listings are public and indexed.
Opens a listing and sees the provider's 'Licensed LLM Data Provider' badge, the trust rating, price, licence, AI-training rights, delivery method, format and updated date.
Reads the licence before buying; to download a sample, the buyer must register and complete onboarding.
Clicks 'Buy Now' (or 'Download' for free items), accepts the provider's licence at checkout and pays through a third-party processor; no refunds once access is granted.
Receives the data by instant download, or the provider delivers it by S3, API, cloud credentials or a negotiated method.
Holds a licence from the provider, not Opendatabay. Under the AI licences the buyer must not redistribute and must delete the data on request or termination.
If nothing fits: submits 'Request a Dataset' with a timeline, and Opendatabay's provider network sources or creates the data.

unknowns.note: Exclusivity appears only as provider-to-broker exclusive brokerage; the pricing article is a placeholder.
Only a last-updated date; nothing on versions, or on what one-off buyers get after an update or withdrawal.
No commissioned-work carve-out; the only change mechanism is unilateral update on continued use. No history of term changes reachable (Wayback blocked, no search).
Who assigns the 'Universal Data Trust Rating' and how is not documented in the docs index or resources hub.
No model-release, property-release or depicted-person clause; the egocentric video and portrait listings are silent; the creator guide is a placeholder.
Buyer article is a placeholder; no sales figures. No independent press could be found without web search.
No web search this run; no press page on the site. The accounts PDF to 31 May 2025 (total exemption) was not opened.
Whether subscribers keep delivered data after cancelling is not addressed.
'Instant download' listings do not say whether files sit on Opendatabay storage or the provider's.
Fee schedule says the rate is determined progressively within a band; the calculator is script-driven and fetched text shows no method, so marginal vs interpolated is unknown.

conflicts.resolution: Onboarding docs, provider agreement and ToS all restrict selling to registered businesses; the about-page line is marketing.
Same as above: the terms bar individual sellers.
The same listing shows a CC0 label and an AI-training-rights text banning redistribution; which governs is not stated.
ToS names arbitration; the Brokerage & Listing Terms name the London courts. Different documents and parties, so both may apply.

leads.why: Total exemption accounts to 31 May 2025 (PDF) would give balance-sheet scale; not opened.
Egocentric-data article under the robotics hub; hub page itself showed only titles.
